title: Aaron Beck, the son of Jewish immigrants, developed cognitive behavioral therapy for depression and anxiety

trailer.text: Dr. Aaron Beck, the son of Jewish immigrants from Providence, revolutionized psychiatry when he developed cognitive behavioral therapy.
Like other psychiatrists of his time, he was trained in Freud's ideas, but in his patients he did not find much pent-up anger, and he found a great deal of negative thinking about themselves.
According to the Lasker Foundation, by 1961 he had left psychoanalysis and taught patients to identify and challenge distorted thoughts.
According to the Lasker Foundation, in 1977 he tested the method against an antidepressant, and the therapy outperformed the drug.
Today the therapy is used for depression, anxiety, eating disorders and addiction, and according to The New York Times it is the most studied form of psychotherapy in the world.

glance.label: Studies
glance.value: More than 2,000 on the therapy's effectiveness, according to the Inquirer

paragraphs.text: Aaron Beck was born in Providence, Rhode Island, in July 1921.
His parents were Jewish immigrants.
According to the obituary in the BJPsych Bulletin, their names were Elizabeth Temkin and Harry Beck, and the father was a printer.
According to the AP, at age 8 Beck was hospitalized, and he became fearful of hospitals and blood.
According to the same report, he overcame the fear on his own, and these were his first cognitive therapy exercises.
He graduated from Brown University in 1942 and from medical school at Yale in 1946.
According to the BMJ, he never intended to become a psychiatrist, and after medical school he did a residency in pathology.
In 1950 he married Phyllis.
In the mid-1950s he settled in Wynnewood, Pennsylvania, to work at Valley Forge Army Hospital.
According to Encyclopedia.com, Aaron Beck was born in Providence, Rhode Island, on July 18, 1921.

stations.title: What did not fit in the therapy room

paragraphs.text: Like other psychiatrists in the mid-20th century, Beck was trained in Freud's ideas.
One of them said that depression is anger that a person turns against himself.
According to the Lasker Foundation, Freud's psychoanalytic theory dominated psychiatry at the time.
According to the Inquirer, Beck found little evidence that his patients were angry inside.
According to the same source, what he found in them was negative, irrational thinking about themselves.
According to the Lasker Foundation, he did not find hostility in the dreams of depressed patients either.
According to the foundation, he saw that in their dreams they saw themselves as they did during the day: hopeless and helpless.
According to the Lasker Foundation, Beck realized something else: if patients are concerned with what the therapist thinks of them, there is no point in waiting for unconscious thoughts to surface.

stations.title: The thoughts that come before the emotion

paragraphs.text: According to the Lasker Foundation, by 1961 Beck had left psychoanalysis.
According to the foundation, he began to focus on the moments when patients felt bad, and on the thoughts that appeared just before the emotion.
According to The New York Times, he discovered that many people generated what he called automatic thoughts.
According to the Lasker Foundation, Beck realized that a person's negative, unrealistic image of himself feeds mental disorders.
According to the foundation, he taught patients to identify the distorted thoughts and to challenge them.
According to the AP, cognitive therapy holds that the key is to turn around the inner monologue that disparages the person, often in a dozen sessions or fewer.
According to the AP, he developed the method at the University of Pennsylvania in the 1960s.
According to the BMJ, the therapy usually takes place once a week, for half an hour to an hour, and only rarely lasts more than a few months.
In 1961 the Beck Depression Inventory was also developed, a 21-question questionnaire that the person fills out himself.
The questionnaire remains a leading test for measuring the severity of depression.
Beck said that he had no training in research methods or statistics, and so he asked himself how he could obtain evidence.
According to his account, his friend Marvin Stein helped him design a study and prepare a grant application.
According to The New York Times, for years Beck worked almost unnoticed, unsure of his path, and supported mainly by his wife, Phyllis.
According to the Lasker Foundation, in 1977 Beck conducted the first rigorous clinical trial of any kind of psychotherapy for depression.
The trial compared cognitive therapy with the drug imipramine.
Beck said that one of his residents at the time, John Rush, conducted the clinical trial, and that Beck himself trained other residents in the therapy.

According to the Lasker Foundation, in a head-to-head comparison cognitive therapy outperformed the drug after a treatment period of up to 12 weeks, and the benefit of the therapy persisted a year later as well.
According to Hollon, research has generally found the therapy to be at least as effective as medications for non-psychotic disorders, and its results last longer.
According to the Inquirer, today there are more than 2,000 studies of the therapy's effectiveness, and it is the most studied non-drug mental health treatment.
According to the Lasker Foundation, in a seven-year study of 1,958 outpatients, Beck's hopelessness test identified 16 of the 17 people who killed themselves.
Beck and his colleagues tested cognitive therapy in people who had already attempted suicide.
According to the Lasker Foundation, those who received cognitive therapy were almost 50 percent less likely to attempt suicide during an 18-month follow-up.
According to EBSCO, Beck served as the director of the Aaron Beck Psychopathology Research Center, founded in 1998 for suicide prevention research.

stations.title: The idea goes out into the world

paragraphs.text: According to the obituary in the BJPsych Bulletin, in the 1980s and 1990s cognitive behavioral therapy largely replaced psychoanalysis as the leading psychological theory.
According to the AP, it became required training for psychiatry residents.
According to the Inquirer, it is used today for depression, anxiety, eating and personality disorders, and addiction.
According to the Lasker Foundation, health systems in Europe recommend the therapy for a number of common psychiatric disorders.
According to the foundation, the Labour government in Britain committed to training 10,000 therapists, so that at least one million patients could receive the therapy.
The British IAPT program, which is built on the principles of the therapy, is still widely used.
In 1994 Beck and his daughter, Dr. Judith Beck, founded the Beck Institute in Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania.
According to EBSCO, in 2007 Beck launched the Beck Initiative in Philadelphia, a training program in cognitive therapy.
City of Philadelphia agencies were partners in this initiative.
Later in life Beck conducted revolutionary research on patients with schizophrenia, a group long neglected by the psychiatric establishment.
According to JTA, he realized that his usual approach did not work with them, and he encouraged them to focus on the times when they were at their best.
According to the Beck Institute, Recovery-Oriented Cognitive Therapy (CT-R) was originally developed to empower people diagnosed with serious mental health conditions such as schizophrenia.
According to the Lasker Foundation, at the age of 85 Beck received two research grants from the NIH.
Beck won the Heinz Award in 2001 and the Lasker Award for Clinical Medical Research in 2006.
He also received the Gustave O. Lienhard Award from the Institute of Medicine.
According to EBSCO, on October 23, 2013 he became the first person to receive the Kennedy Community Health Award.
Yale, the University of Pennsylvania and Brown awarded him honorary degrees.
According to Seligman, he was short-listed for the Nobel Prize but did not win it.
American Psychologist magazine named him among the most influential psychotherapists ever.
According to J Clin Psychiatry, a 2016 Medscape peer survey determined that Beck was the fourth most influential person in the history of medicine.
According to the Beck Institute, in 2005 and 2014 he held public and private dialogues with the Dalai Lama.
According to Hollon of Vanderbilt University, Beck took a hundred-year-old dogma, found that it did not hold up, and invented something brief, lasting and effective in its place.
According to DeRubeis, he can perhaps be regarded as the most important figure in mental health in the last century.
Beck died on November 1, 2021 at his home in Philadelphia, at the age of 100.
Beck's funeral was held on November 3 at the synagogue Temple Beth Hillel-Beth El in Wynnewood, where he held the status of lifetime member.
He was survived by his wife Phyllis, four children, 10 grandchildren and 10 great-grandchildren.
According to Grant, many colleagues rejected Beck's ideas until he was over 50.
According to Grant, few came to his early talks, and psychoanalysts dismissed him.
Because of his views and his way of working, the American Psychoanalytic Institute refused to certify him.
According to the AP, some psychologists said that cognitive therapy was superficial and no more than a morale booster.
According to the AP, Beck published much of his work in his own journal, partly because other professionals disregarded his findings.
Even today, not everything is settled.
The British IAPT program has critics.

claims.text: ד״ר אהרן בק, שחולל מהפכה בפסיכיאטריה בפיתוח הטיפול הקוגניטיבי-התנהגותי, מת ב-1 בנובמבר בביתו בפילדלפיה.
claims.quote: Dr. Aaron T. Beck, who revolutionized psychiatry by developing the field of cognitive behavioral therapy, died on Nov. 1 at his home in Philadelphia.

claims.text: בק, יליד פרובידנס, היה ילד של מהגרים יהודים מרוסיה.
claims.quote: A native of Providence, Rhode Island, Beck was the child of Russian Jewish immigrants.

claims.text: לפי ההספד ב-BJPsych Bulletin, הוריו של בק, אליזבת טמקין והארי בק (מדפיס), היו מהגרים יהודים מאוקראינה.
claims.quote: His parents, Elizabeth Temkin and Harry Beck, a printer, were Jewish immigrants from Ukraine.

claims.text: כמו פסיכיאטרים אחרים באמצע המאה ה-20, בק הוכשר במושגים פרוידיאניים, ובהם הרעיון שדיכאון הוא תוצאה של כעס המופנה פנימה.
claims.quote: Like other psychiatrists in the mid-20th century, Dr. Beck was trained in Freudian concepts, including the idea that depression was the result of anger turned inward.

claims.text: לפי ה-Inquirer, בק מצא ראיות מועטות לכך שמטופליו כועסים בתוכם, אך הם סבלו מחשיבה שלילית ולא רציונלית על עצמם.
claims.quote: He found little evidence that his patients were angry inside, but they did suffer from negative, irrational thinking about themselves.

claims.text: לפי קרן לסקר, עד 1961 בק זנח את הפסיכואנליזה והתמקד ברגעים שבהם מטופלים חשו רע ובמחשבות שקדמו לרגש.
claims.quote: By 1961, Beck had abandoned psychoanalysis. Instead, he was zeroing in on particular instances in which patients felt bad and asking what thoughts immediately preceded the uncomfortable emotion.

claims.text: לפי קרן לסקר, בק הבין שתפיסות עצמיות שליליות לא מציאותיות מזינות הפרעות נפשיות, ולימד מטופלים לזהות מחשבות מעוותות ולערער עליהן.
claims.quote: By realizing that unrealistic negative self-perceptions foster such disturbances and then teaching patients to identify and challenge these distorted thoughts

claims.text: לפי קרן לסקר, ב-1977 בק ערך את הניסוי הקליני הקפדני הראשון בכל סוג של פסיכותרפיה לדיכאון, והשווה טיפול קוגניטיבי לאימיפרמין.
claims.quote: He compared the effectiveness of cognitive therapy to imipramine (the best antidepressant at the time).

claims.text: לפי קרן לסקר, בהשוואה ישירה הטיפול הקוגניטיבי עקף את התרופה לאחר עד 12 שבועות, והיתרונות נמשכו שנה לאחר מכן.
claims.quote: In this head-to-head comparison, cognitive therapy outperformed the drug after a treatment period of up to 12 weeks. Furthermore, the benefits persisted a year later.

claims.text: לפי ה-Inquirer, הטיפול הקוגניטיבי-התנהגותי משמש כיום למגוון רחב של מחלות נפש, ובהן דיכאון, הפרעות אכילה ואישיות, חרדה והתמכרות.
claims.quote: CBT is now used for a wide variety of mental illnesses, including depression, eating and personality disorders, anxiety, and addiction.

claims.text: לפי הניו יורק טיימס, בעשורים האחרונים הטיפול הקוגניטיבי-התנהגותי הפך לצורת הפסיכותרפיה הנחקרת ביותר בעולם.
claims.quote: Over the past several decades, CBT has become by far the world's most extensively studied form of psychotherapy.

claims.text: לפי ה-AP, בק פיתח את הטיפול הקוגניטיבי באוניברסיטת פנסילבניה בשנות ה-60.
claims.quote: Beck developed the field of cognitive therapy, a clinical form of psychotherapy, at the University of Pennsylvania in the 1960s.

claims.text: בק ובתו ג׳ודי בק ייסדו ב-1994 את מכון בק בבאלה סינווייד, פנסילבניה.

claims.quote: With more than 2,000 studies of its impact, CBT is the most studied non-drug mental health treatment.

claims.quote: according to the Beck Institute for Cognitive Behavior Therapy, which he co-founded with his daughter, Dr. Judith Beck

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, ב-2007 בק השיק בפילדלפיה את תוכנית ההכשרה Beck Initiative בטיפול קוגניטיבי.
claims.quote: in 2007 he launched the Beck Initiative Training Program in Cognitive Therapy in Philadelphia

claims.text: בק זוכה לקרדיט על הקמת יוזמת בק בשיתוף סוכנויות של עיריית פילדלפיה.
claims.quote: Beck is also credited with founding the Beck Initiative in collaboration with City of Philadelphia agencies.

claims.text: בהמשך חייו בק ערך מחקר מהפכני על מטופלי סכיזופרניה, שהממסד הפסיכיאטרי הזניח זמן רב.
claims.quote: Later in life, Beck also delivered revolutionary research on schizophrenic patients, who had long been written off by the psychiatric establishment.

claims.text: לפי JTA, בק הבין שגישתו הרגילה לא עבדה עם מטופלי סכיזופרניה, ולכן היה עליו לעודד אותם להתמקד ברגעים שבהם היו במיטבם.
claims.quote: Instead, he had to motivate them to focus on times when they were at their best.

claims.text: לפי מכון בק, הטיפול הקוגניטיבי ממוקד ההחלמה (CT-R) פותח במקור כדי להעצים אנשים עם אבחנות של מצבי בריאות נפש קשים כמו סכיזופרניה.
claims.quote: Originally developed to empower individuals given a diagnosis of serious mental health conditions such as schizophrenia

claims.text: לפי קרן לסקר, בגיל 85 בק קיבל שני מענקי NIH לתמיכה במחקרו.
claims.quote: Thus it is not surprising that at the age of 85 years he received two NIH grants to support his research.

claims.text: בק קיבל את פרס Gustave O. Lienhard של מכון הרפואה.
claims.quote: the Gustave O. Lienhard Award from the Institute of Medicine

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, ב-23 באוקטובר 2013 בק הפך לאדם הראשון שקיבל את פרס קנדי לבריאות הקהילה.
claims.quote: he became the first person to receive the Kennedy Community Health Award

claims.text: בק קיבל תארי כבוד מיייל, מאוניברסיטת פנסילבניה ומבראון.
claims.quote: He received honorary degrees from Yale University, the University of Pennsylvania and Brown University.

claims.text: לפי סליגמן, בק היה ברשימה הקצרה לפרס נובל אך לא זכה בו.
claims.quote: Seligman said that Dr. Beck was, in fact, short-listed for that award but did not win it.

claims.text: לפי מכון בק, ה-American Psychologist כינה אותו אחד מחמשת הפסיכותרפיסטים המשפיעים ביותר בכל הזמנים.
claims.quote: one of the five most influential psychotherapists of all time

claims.text: לפי ה-AP, ב-1982 המגזין American Psychologist מנה את בק בין עשרת הפסיכותרפיסטים המשפיעים ביותר אי פעם.
claims.quote: American Psychologist magazine in 1982 named Beck one of the 10 most influential psychotherapists ever.

claims.text: לפי סקר עמיתים של Medscape ב-2016, בק היה הרביעי בהשפעתו בהיסטוריה של הרפואה.
claims.quote: a peer-based survey conducted by the continuing medical education giant Medscape in 2016 determined that Professor Beck was the fourth most influential person in the history of medicine.

claims.text: לפי מכון בק, ב-2005 וב-2014 בק קיים דיאלוגים פומביים ופרטיים עם הדלאי לאמה.
claims.quote: In 2005 and 2014, he engaged in public and private dialogues with the Dalai Lama.

claims.text: לפי הולון מאוניברסיטת ונדרבילט, בק לקח מאה שנות דוגמה, גילה שהיא לא עומדת במבחן והמציא תחתיה משהו קצר, מתמשך ויעיל.
claims.quote: He took a hundred years of dogma, found that it didn't hold up, and invented something brief, lasting and effective to put in its place.

claims.text: לפי דה-רוביס, ניתן לראות בבק אולי את הדמות החשובה ביותר בבריאות הנפש במאה האחרונה.
claims.quote: I would put him as arguably the most important figure in mental health in the last century

claims.text: לפי JTA, בק נולד ב-18 ביולי 1921 והגיע לגיל 100 בשנת מותו.
claims.quote: Born on July 18, 1921, he turned 100 earlier this year.

claims.text: לפי ה-Inquirer, בק מת ביום שני בדירתו בכיכר ריטנהאוס בגיל 100.
claims.quote: Dr. Beck, who died Monday at his Rittenhouse Square condominium at the age of 100

claims.text: הלווייתו של בק נערכה ב-3 בנובמבר בבית הכנסת Temple Beth Hillel-Beth El בווינווד, שבו היה חבר לכל החיים.
claims.quote: on Nov. 3 at Temple Beth Hillel-Beth El in Wynnewood, where he was a lifetime member

claims.text: בק הותיר אישה, פיליס, ארבעה ילדים, 10 נכדים ו-10 נינים.
claims.quote: Aaron Beck is survived by his wife, Phyllis; children Roy, Judith, Daniel and Alice; 10 grandchildren; and 10 great-grandchildren.

claims.text: לפי גרנט, רעיונותיו של בק נדחו על ידי עמיתים רבים עד גיל 50 ויותר, מעטים הגיעו להרצאותיו המוקדמות והפסיכואנליטיקאים פטרו אותו.
claims.quote: his ideas were rejected by many of his peers until he was over 50. Few came to his early talks. Psychoanalysts dismissed him.

claims.text: בגלל דעותיו הלא-שגרתיות ופרקטיקה הקלינית שלו, בק נדחה להסמכה על ידי המכון הפסיכואנליטי האמריקאי.
claims.quote: He received his psychoanalytic training at the Philadelphia Institute but, having completed training, because of his unorthodox views and clinical practice, was rejected for certification by the American Psychoanalytic Institute.

claims.text: לפי ה-AP, בק פרסם חלק גדול מעבודתו בכתב העת שלו, בין היתר מפני שאנשי מקצוע אחרים התעלמו מממצאיו.
claims.quote: He published much of his work in his own journal, Cognitive Therapy and Research, partly because other mental health professionals disregarded his findings.

claims.text: לפי תומס, עדיין לא ברור אם הטיפול ממוקד ההחלמה יהיה בעל השפעה על אנשים עם סכיזופרניה כמו זו של הטיפול הקוגניטיבי על דיכאון.
claims.quote: Although it is not yet clear if recovery-oriented CBT will have the magnitude of impact for people with schizophrenia

claims.text: לפי ה-AP, בק היה הבן השלישי להורים מהגרים יהודים רוסים ממעמד הביניים.
claims.quote: A native of Providence, R.I., and the third son of middle-class Russian Jewish immigrants

claims.text: לפי JTA, בק כתב יותר מ-600 מאמרים מדעיים ו-25 ספרים.
claims.quote: Beck had authored more than 600 scholarly articles and 25 books, ranking him as the fourth-most influential medical practitioner within the past century.

claims.text: לפי ה-AP, בק כתב או שותף לכתיבת 17 ספרים ופרסם יותר מ-500 מאמרים.
claims.quote: He wrote or co-wrote 17 books, published more than 500 articles

claims.text: לפי Encyclopedia.com, אהרן בק נולד בפרובידנס שברוד איילנד ב-18 ביולי 1921.
claims.quote: Aaron T. Beck was born in Providence, Rhode Island, on July 18, 1921
